item.title: Re: Update 5/17/16
item.content:encoded: Chiming in to add that while The Analog Kid brings the Anderson tales into the continuity of Third Law, it doesn't necessarily bring Third Law into continuity with the Anderson tales. It's entirely possible to just ignore the rest of Third Law while still using The Analog Kid, just like it's possible to use the magic system that Clef establishes in the GOC Casefiles canon without using the rest of that canon.

item.content:encoded: Maybe it is confusing. But the end product of electronic telepathy is just too cool to pass up.

item.title: Re: Update 5/17/16
item.content:encoded: That's fair. I didn't mean to insinuate that it was the end-all be-all, just that placing the tale in a timeline made it a bit confusing.

item.title: Re: Update 5/17/16
item.content:encoded:
Currently I would argue that the GoI and the canon are not any more tied together than MC&D is tied to any of the canons it appears in. Authors are free to use AR inside canons, outside canons, upside canons, and downside canons, and all relations to canons between.

The timeline on the final tab is merely the chronological order for the over arcing plot shared by the majority of AR tales, and should be seen no more as the end all be all version of AR than Resurrection is the end all be all story for this wiki.

item.title: Re: Update 5/17/16
item.content:encoded: If the tale is set in a canon though (as the author comment on that page indicates), and it's included in the timeline, wouldn't that indicate that the canon and the GoI are tied together? What if someone wants to write the GoI outside of that canon? Or am I reading too much into that?

Even the "blew themselves up" part isn't necessarily a sign of incompetence:The PEPCON disaster, for instance, involved one of the US government's trusted producers of solid rocket fuel, which had been competently handling some of the most volatile substances on Earth for decades. They're still not entirely sure what set it off1 but the end result was a series of some of the most energetic uncontrolled chemical explosions in recorded history, approximately 1 kiloton TNT equivalent.

Footnotes
1. getting forced by the government into storing literal tons more Ammonium Perchlorate than their facilities were designed to, the local gas company deciding that "poorly maintained high pressure gas main" and "limited flow pipe" were basically the same thing, and workers having no choice but to repair critical structural damage from a windstorm by welding near the storage area all may have played a part.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Well, the business angle is also covered partially by The Factory and Doctor Wondertainment, in addition to AR, MC&D, and PL.

Just as we have five religiously based GoIs: MC, HI, CotBG, Sarkcism, and Fifth Church.

And just as we have three local government GoIs: UIU, GRU-P, and ORIA.

My point with all this is that the GoI list has a ton of overlap in terms of the basic themes of what each group does. In my opinion, thats okay. In the vast anomalous world of the SCP universe the GoIs bleed into each other to create a rich fabric of characters, ideas, and organizations, rather than multiple boxes that are kept separate from each other.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I regard the similarity between AR and CotBG (specifically Cogwork Orthodoxy) to be the focus on machinery and robotics-based technology. Since the gentlemen below brought up PL, the difference is clear: PL is a broad contender who tries all, while AR (obviously) specialises in the specific domain of anomalous robotics.

Of course, one could easily say that CotBG applies religious meaning to the machine whereas AR applies business potential to it. Of which, the business angle is fairly covered by the PL format and MC&D.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: Anderson is nothing like CotBG. The closest group to it is Prometheus Labs, in that both are paratech firms. Anderson differs in that there are clear resemblances to a modern-day Silicon Valley tech startup (as opposed to PL which is more akin to an IBM or Lockheed), and it's also not weighed down by the prevalent "lol we blew ourselves up" incompetence of many PL portrayals.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: To put it another way, AR is in it for the science and the profit, sort of like their former competitor, Prometheus Labs. Where PL went under due to bad management, over-diversification, and over-investment in large projects with major flaws, Anderson Robotics is a smaller, more focused company that keeps their sights set just slightly beyond what's actually possible. The CotBG are among their major customers, but the difference is sort of like the difference between a wine maker and a Christian denomination that uses wine for communion.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: Well, its not a religion. So that would be a big difference between the two. Whereas the anomalies of the CotBG tend to be pieces of the Broken God, or holy artifacts of the church, the anomalies of AR are simply paratech products meant for sale to an expanding market.

item.content:encoded: Cool, although I am still ambivalent towards how Anderson stands out from other technology-based GoIs. Any recommendations for those who think "How is this different from CotBG"?

item.title: Author Posts are for squares.
item.content:encoded:
Alright! Now that Anderson Robotics is a big time GoI, it needs an official GoI hub. That was the goal I aimed to accomplish here.

Now, there are a few things that this hub is:

  • A means of diving into the Anderson Robotics material for those unfamiliar with it.
  • A spring board for those interested in writing their own Anderson Robotics skip or tale.
  • A chronological listing of the already existing tales in the continuing series.1

There are also a few things this hub is not:

  • A canon.
  • A means of me to tell new writers what they can and cannot do with these characters.2

That being said, some serious thanks are in order.

Thank you A Random Day, GreenWolf, djkaktus, TwistedGears, TyGently, ProcyonLotor, Doctor Cimmerian, Metaphysician, and minmin for your help with feedback on this hub. It was very much appreciated.

Special Thank You to Decibelles, TwistedGears, djkaktus, Kalinin, and Doctor Cimmerian for your contributions to the success of this GoI. You each added your own flavor to the concept, and the end products have been so much fun to read.

Finally, an extra special bonus thank you to SunnyClockwork for creating the slick new Anderson Robotics logo. You are the real MVP.

Enjoy the hub.

Conwell

Footnotes
1. See the Investigative Timeline tab.
2. Seriously, it’s an established GoI now guys. Go nuts.
